findings.evidence: Description covers WHAT, WHEN, keywords and the feedback-mastery boundary, but not the written follow-up and check-in the body requires
findings.fix: Prepare, rehearse and follow up on high-stakes workplace conversations where the outcome is negotiated, facts are disputed, the news is bad, or emotions may derail it, including the written summary and dated check-in. Use for asking for a raise, salary, promotion or workload terms; delivering a layoff, role elimination or other bad news; a clash after public criticism or a blowup; mediating a dispute between others whose accounts of the facts conflict; raising a sensitive personal concern (health, family), harassment, or threats at work; deciding whether you are calm enough to talk; repairing after getting defensive; or writing the follow-up note and check-in after one of these, even if the user never says 'difficult conversation'. Not for feedback on a specific behavior (including to each person in a conflict you lead), recognition, replying to vague criticism, scope or deadline pushback, or feedback recaps (use feedback-mastery); not for legal advice, drafting formal complaints, PIPs, ratings, policy, or company-wide announcements.

findings.evidence: "I'll need longer" points at SKILL.md Section 2 and also at the buying-time line in emotional-regulation.md, which Section 2 does not load
